items.headline: Marvell to buy Lumentum in $80B all-stock AI deal
items.summary: Marvell Technology agreed to acquire Lumentum in an all-stock transaction worth roughly $80 billion, combining two fast-growing enablers of AI connectivity. The deal positions the combined company as a leader in the infrastructure underpinning AI data centers.

items.headline: Morgan Stanley CEO sees up to $15T AI investment wave
items.summary: Morgan Stanley CEO Ted Pick suggested AI investment could reach $10 trillion to $15 trillion over the next decade, driven by expected productivity gains. The forecast underscores the scale of capital flowing into AI infrastructure amid market jitters.

items.headline: OpenAI hires ex-Army Secretary Dan Driscoll for national security
items.summary: OpenAI appointed former U.S. Army Secretary Dan Driscoll as Senior Counselor for National Security Modernization to help expand AI use in national and cyber security. The hire signals the AI lab's deepening push into defense and government markets.

items.headline: Anthropic posts $17B Q3 revenue as IPO approaches
items.summary: Anthropic revealed its quarterly revenue reached $17 billion, up more than 12-fold year-over-year, while its net loss totaled $23 billion. The surging figures come as the company prepares for a landmark public offering.

items.headline: Anthropic warns it's 'very close' to self-improving AI
items.summary: In its IPO prospectus, Anthropic warned that its increasing use of AI to accelerate its own R&D could cause model capabilities to advance faster than its safety measures. The company said it may imminently meet thresholds for recursive self-improvement capability.

items.headline: Oracle files to sell $20B in stock and bonds for AI
items.summary: Oracle filed plans to issue $10 billion in common stock and $10 billion in senior notes to finance its AI data-center buildout. Shares fell 3% in premarket trading amid investor concerns about the hyperscaler's mounting debt.

items.headline: UK warned to expect AI-powered attack on infrastructure
items.summary: A report said the UK must expect an AI-powered attack on critical infrastructure within two years, with AI-enhanced malware 'highly likely' to be used against national systems. The warning highlights escalating cybersecurity risks posed by advancing AI tools.

items.headline: BofA warns AI boom poses major risk to global economy
items.summary: Bank of America cautioned that a sustained correction in the AI trade represents a major risk to the global economy, as data-center backlash framed the 2026 midterm vote. The warning landed the day before Americans headed to the polls.

items.headline: OpenAI plans next internal security sprint to harden systems
items.summary: OpenAI announced a new internal security sprint, partnering with Cathedral Systems to use its own models to test and strengthen its systems. The effort reflects growing urgency around securing frontier AI infrastructure against sophisticated threats.

items.headline: AI data centers emerge as key 2026 midterm election issue
items.summary: Some 84% of 49 AI data center-related ballot measures across 13 states will be decided in the November midterms, with Ohio alone having 21 measures. Candidates in 20 gubernatorial races are also calling for moratoriums on data center development.

items.headline: Meta taps euro bond market to fund AI investments
items.summary: Meta issued euro-denominated bonds to finance its AI buildout, following Alphabet and Amazon which have issued roughly 29.5 billion euros in euro bonds this year. European institutional capital is increasingly flowing toward US AI infrastructure.

items.headline: Chipmaker selloff deepens, Nasdaq 100 enters correction
items.summary: A gauge of chipmakers extended a three-day rout to 12% and the Nasdaq 100 sank 10% from its peak, entering a technical correction. The selloff reflects mounting investor anxiety over the sustainability of AI capital spending.

items.headline: Microsoft president says AI less regulated than milk
items.summary: Microsoft president Brad Smith warned that AI is currently less regulated than milk, arguing voluntary commitments by tech giants are necessary but no longer sufficient. His remarks followed a White House meeting where AI leaders signed a 'morally binding' document.

items.headline: AustralianSuper sticks to AI 'picks and shovels' amid turbulence
items.summary: Australia's largest pension fund said it will stick to chipmakers and hyperscaler data centers as it navigates unprecedented turbulence in global tech stocks. The A$430 billion fund believes these 'picks and shovels' will weather the current AI sector storm.

items.headline: Google launches Gemini 4 Argon for hardest problems
items.summary: Google introduced Gemini 4 Argon, the first of its Gemini 4 model family, designed for complex engineering, cybersecurity, and scientific problems. The model is priced at $4 per 1M input tokens and $20 per 1M output tokens after an introductory period ending November 30, 2026.

items.headline: AI chatbots become major source of 2026 election information
items.summary: The 2026 midterms mark the first federal election where tens of millions of voters get political information from generative AI tools. Nearly 40% of survey respondents reported getting election info from Google's AI-search summaries.

items.headline: OpenAI's Terra model reaches AWS Bedrock at low price
items.summary: OpenAI's newest Terra model arrived on Amazon Bedrock priced well below the model beside it, alongside GPT-6.1 availability. The additions expand the range of frontier models accessible to AWS enterprise customers.

items.headline: Anthropic updates usage policy on model abuse and risks
items.summary: Anthropic updated its Usage Policy, adding a prohibition on sustained, needless cruelty toward its models and aligning with its feature allowing Claude to end abusive conversations. The update reflects evolving thinking on model welfare and safety as capabilities grow.

items.headline: OpenAI publishes updated Model Spec for capable AI
items.summary: OpenAI released an updated Model Spec defining how its models should behave to be more capable and beneficial, alongside new research on detecting frontier model misalignment. The updates aim to improve transparency and safety as models become more powerful.

items.headline: Nature Machine Intelligence calls for meaningful AI versioning
items.summary: Researchers argued in Nature Machine Intelligence that AI needs meaningful versioning to support regulatory oversight and scientific reproducibility. The paper highlights gaps in how rapidly changing AI models are documented and tracked.
